# Brad Devices

> The entire computer stack — silicon, GPU, memory, OS, software — designed as one spec by Festus Bradley Nyadimo (By BradVerse), a 15-year-old building from Africa. Software ships before silicon: every SHIPPED part below is a real file tree that runs today and is verified unattended in CI.

## What this site actually is

Every claim on this site carries one of three receipts, and a tag that states exactly what a file can prove today:

- SOLID / SHIPPED — the software or document exists, opens today, and runs unattended in CI.
- DESIGNED — the silicon is fully registered and specced; production is a fab step.
- VISION — honest future physics, labeled as such.

Nothing is dressed up beyond its tag: no invented benchmarks, no pretend silicon. The product line puts every device in a tier (SHIPPED / DESIGNED / VISION) with the file tree to prove it.

## Provides

- The one book: a 1,737-line unified compendium (eleven parts, 0–10 plus appendices, 120 documents) covering chips, GPUs, memory, OS, compute, software, console and roadmap — every register accounted for, with Gen 1 / Gen 2 / Vision tagging. Ships as a 41-page branded PDF.
- BradVector — the GPU/accelerator instruction-set architecture (dual-issue SIMT, 32-thread warps) that every Torox die runs: BradFx (integrated), BradGfx (dedicated), BradApex (datacenter). It is a separate ISA from the CPU-side BradISA; the two meet on the BradFusion fabric and share memory (SPMP), not instructions.
- The Torox GPU family — BFT100 (integrated), BGT100 (dedicated), BAT100 (datacenter) — one die name, three jobs, one ISA from phone to rack.
- The unified memory model — SPMP (DRAM pool) + BradRAM (JEDEC dies with the L4 SRAM assistant cache on the controller) + the Infinity Buffer, zero-copy between CPU, GPU and NPU.
- BradSense-Render — the GPU reconstruction engine. Status: M0 SHIPPED as a software reference, M1–M4 queued. The spatial core is real: bilinear + Catmull-Rom bicubic upscale at arbitrary ratio, luma-adaptive sharpen with an anti-ringing clamp and a flat-region gate, fed into `bradsense_reconstruct()` via `bradsense_supply_frame()`, returning -ENODATA rather than inventing pixels. Receipt: `src/tests/test_bradsense_pixels.c` in the ctest suite; 2× super-resolution PSNR 39.43 dB (bilinear) / 39.44 dB (bicubic) / 39.57 dB (bicubic + sharpen), byte-deterministic, per-pixel anti-ringing bound verified. Queued: M1 temporal core (history buffer, motion-vector reprojection, responsive masks), M2 the metrics harness that makes it repeatable, M3 expressing the temporal core as BradVector kernels, M4 the trained per-object semantic experts. Honest framing: "we use AI to upscale" is the floor — FSR 4, DLSS 4 and XeSS 2 are all ML; the claim is the object-aware semantic pipeline. The algorithm is FSR-3-derived but reimplemented from published behaviour (AMD's FidelityFX SDK is MIT), never cargo-copied and never branded FSR. The product stays Design/Sil in the registry; only the software reference ships.
- BradOS and the Kinetic and Torox drivers across Mobile, Slate, Compute and Nano.
- The social profiles — every public account with the avatar each platform actually serves:
  3 of 4 profiles readable from outside and shown verbatim, the fourth (LinkedIn) marked unverifiable
  rather than illustrated, because it serves a login wall: https://brad-devices.vercel.app/social/
- The journal — 22 founder essays archived verbatim in order, 2025 to 2026, each
  with its date, read time, word count and cover, plus the posts published since as the platform's own
  preview (text and image fetched, never retyped, no engagement counts):
  https://brad-devices.vercel.app/journal/
- Selected writing by the founder — 22 essays on Medium. The most recent is
  "The Receipts, One Year Later" (2026-10-07): an account of the build with every figure linked to its
  receipt — https://medium.com/@bradleynyadimo/the-receipts-one-year-later-7fb289051805
- The shipped reference toolchain — assembler, interpreter, debugger, profiler, one-binary dev CLI, host API, and browser wasm build.
  Released as v0.1.0 (MIT) with prebuilt binaries for linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64 and macos-arm64, each with a sha256: https://github.com/Brad-Devices/BradVector/releases/tag/v0.1.0 The release job refuses to publish unless ctest is green (24 tests in the tree today — the live count is site/assets/facts.json).
- BradDev Kit, TIFA AI toolchain, and BMS cloud services — all stdlib-only, all runnable today.
- ANF — BradXon's Adaptive Neural Fabric: compute partitions (MIG-class), a reconfigurable dataflow NPU (CGRA-class), and a fabric governor that steers clock/power/bandwidth. It adapts budget, not silicon — DESIGNED Gen 1; the literal unit-morph stays VISION.

## The reference toolchain (SHIPPED, runs today)

- bradc — the BradVector assembler. Parses .bvbs, validates, emits portable .bvbc bytecode; rejects bad code with line-level errors. Behavior pinned by round-trip bytecode tests; a 10-insn saxpy confirmed.
- BVRT — a 32-lane SIMT virtual machine that interprets .bvbc; runs vector saxpy across all 32 lanes and checks every result.
- bradgdb — the debugger. Attach, set an instruction breakpoint, inspect registers and the program counter.
- BradTimeline — cycle-level trace engine exporting full instruction traces to CSV.
- braddev — the one-binary dev CLI (cvt / run / dbg / gpu info / gpu top / timeline / test) built on the shipped stack plus SPMP / EROE / Fabric drivers. All self-checks pass; saxpy and fib run end-to-end.
- bradlib.h — the stable host-facing BradVector Platform API (compile → pack → session → launch → run → inspect → breakpoints), exposed 1:1 to the browser via site/js/bradvector.js.
- BVLibs — the reference math + neural libraries (BVML: saxpy, dot, gemm; BVN: relu, affine, softmax, gelu, silu). Public boundary: API headers, .bvbs kernels, tests, and an independent host reference — repo Brad-Devices/BVLibs; run live in the site's wasm via BradVector.lib.*.
- TIFA SDK — Python-first AI toolchain (import tifa): one-line optimize(), AutoNeuroStream partition (BNV / BVX / BFX), MoE expert spooler, exact FP8/FP4/INT4 digit formats.
- BMS — Brad Mobile Services: REST spec + stdlib-only reference server — BradID auth, BradMail, BradHub, BradPay ledger, BradCloud, BradNotify, BradGeo.

## The stack — one machine, six parts

- Silicon: BradChip fuses CPU + GPU + NPU + the custom BradFusion fabric on one package (tiers Lite P2+E4 → Max P8+E8; Torox GPU; up to 1024-core NPU). BradXon is the flagship whose Adaptive Neural Fabric — compute partitions, a reconfigurable dataflow NPU, a fabric governor — steers power, clock, and fabric budget to the workload. One fabric crosses every die — no PCIe-style borders.
- GPU: every Torox die runs the same BradVector engine — write a kernel once, it runs on integrated, discrete and datacenter. BradRT ray-tracing cores and Neuro-Stream AI cores sit on-die. Die registry: BGT = BradGfx (discrete), BFT = BradFx (integrated), BAT = BradApex (datacenter); generation in the number, tier in the suffix (G1 today).
- Memory: BradRAM + SPMP = one unified pool; the GPU is not a guest in a PCIe lane. BradRAM is standard JEDEC LPDDR5X dies plus a Brad-designed controller carrying the L4 SRAM assistant cache, DDS predictive prefetch and inline encryption — no custom DRAM die. SPMP gigabytes of unified LPDDR, Infinity Buffer GPU SRAM, BradSec-RAM encrypted-at-rest regions.
- Systems software: BradOS across Mobile/Slate/Compute/Nano editions (7-year OS updates, 13-year hardware support); the Kinetic and Torox drivers target Vulkan 1.4, DirectX 12 Ultimate, Metal 3, SYCL 2020 — one driver layer, no driver zoo. Both are DESIGNED, not shipped.
- Graphics software: BradSense-Render (above) is the reconstruction engine; Neuro-Stream units are the on-die NPU hardware beside it.
- Products: BradMatrix laptops (Essential → Ultra), BradOS Compute workstations/servers, and the BradAxis console (Torox GPU in a box, Nexus controller) — every product an instance of the same architecture.
- The toolchain above ties all six parts together and ships first.
- The live workbench: https://brad-devices.vercel.app/now/ — what is being built right now, derived from the repository by the build itself.

## Specifications (PDF)

- [The complete Brad Devices spec (41 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/BRAD_DEVICES_COMPLETE_SPEC.pdf): the definitive reference — all registers, encodings and systems in one book.
- [BradGfx architecture (11 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/bradgfx_arch.pdf): the GPU architecture — the six-stage BradVector pipeline and render path drawn as stage diagrams.
- [BradISA (15 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/bradisa_spec.pdf): the ISA — real bit-field figures for RRR / RI / BR / JMP.
- [BradISA v2 vector extension (16 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/bradisa_v2_ext.pdf): 16-bit compressed layout + 256-bit VSET lanes.
- [BradXon platform (17 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/bradxon_platform.pdf): Gen 1 platform — address-layout bands, MMIO, the ANF fabric governor and compute partitions.
- [Brad Devices product portfolio (16 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/product_portfolio.pdf): the full product line — brand-hierarchy tree + software portfolio.
- [Competitive analysis (10 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/competitive_analysis.pdf): whitespace vs the giants — the software-moat line is shipped.
- [BradVector Core vs Intel (8 pages)](https://brad-devices.vercel.app/assets/specs/bradcore_vs_intel.pdf): core-by-core vs the incumbent — benchmark tables, honest rows.

## Key documents in the 120-document design tree

- BradVector ISA — the instruction set every Torox GPU shares (public: github.com/Brad-Devices/BradVector).
- Torox GPU architecture — microarchitecture, die naming, the G1 registry.
- Compute model — kernels, warps, scheduling, shared memory.
- BradChip platform — SoC platforms, boards, cooling, memory modules.
- BradRAM / SPMP — memory die, unified pool, power/security/timing.
- BradOS — the OS across Mobile–Compute editions.
- BradAxis — the console with the Nexus controller.
- Platform strategy — why the shipped toolchain is the moat.

## How to verify

- Read the book: the 41-page PDF or the 1,737-line compendium everything points to.
- Watch it run: the toolchain executes in CI on every push — ctest 24/24 green, the braddev self-test with 0 traps on saxpy and fib, round-trip bytecode tests, and the in-browser wasm build of the platform API.
- Contact: brad.devices.official@gmail.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/Brad-Devices
